transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... it's just getting really hard at work. I make and repair jewelry, you know? And lately, when someone asks me a simple question, like, "When will my ring repair be ready?" I try to answer, but my brain just... goes somewhere else. I'll start talking about their invoice, and then somehow I'm talking about the potting soil I bought for my garden, which reminds me of the mortgage papers I need to sign, and... I just see them staring at me, completely lost. Speaking of the garden, I tried planting some hydrangeas this year, but the soil here is just too acidic, I think. Or maybe it's alkaline? I can never remember which one turns them blue. My grandmother had the most beautiful blue hydrangeas, she used to put rusty nails in the dirt... but anyway, yeah, I just can't seem to keep my thoughts straight when people talk to me.
When did you first begin having difficulty keeping your thoughts straight like this?

Well, this whole change... it's been going on since not long after we took on the business mortgage, so almost two years now. That mortgage process was such a headache. The man at the bank who helped us, he had this really loud ticking clock right on his desk. I noticed it right away because I actually repair vintage pocket watches sometimes along with the jewelry. The tiny gears are just fascinating to me. Though, working with the old silver casings can be tricky because silver tarnishes so quickly if you don't store it right, especially in the humidity. My sister lives down in Florida, and the humidity there is just terrible for tarnishing. She actually wants me to come visit her this winter, but I don't know who would watch my cat. He's very picky about his wet food, he only likes the kind with the gravy... wait, what did you ask me?
Before about two years ago, did you regularly have this same kind of difficulty staying on topic and keeping your thoughts organized?

No, no, before all that started a couple years ago, I was always very sharp. Like I was saying just a minute ago, now I can't even answer a simple question about a ring repair without jumping to invoices and potting soil and seeing the customer just completely lose the thread of what I'm saying. But back then? I was the organized one. 

I had to be, especially with the gemstones. You have to keep everything perfectly sorted in this business. I actually used to organize all our loose stones by the Mohs scale of hardness. You have to do that because if you put a diamond next to a sapphire in a parcel, the diamond will scratch it right up. Sapphires are a nine on the scale, but diamonds are a ten. I had this one client, Mrs. Gable, she brought in the most stunning Montana sapphire for a custom pendant. It had this incredible teal blue color, kind of like the ocean in the winter. I've always wanted to go to the coast in the winter, just to see the waves when it's really stormy and gray out. There's this little bed and breakfast in Oregon my husband and I looked at a brochure for once, and they serve homemade scones every morning with clotted cream. I tried making clotted cream at home once, but you really need unpasteurized milk for it to set right, and that's actually illegal to buy in some places. It’s a shame, really, because the taste in the store-bought jars is just... 

Oh. I'm doing it again, aren't I? I'm sorry. I just... I didn't used to be like this.
Since these difficulties began, have you needed someone else to take over any tasks you previously managed on your own?

Yeah, I have. My husband has had to start double-checking all the invoices for me, which I always used to handle completely by myself. He’s really good with the numbers, though. He actually bought one of those old-school calculators the other day, the kind with the paper roll that makes that loud printing sound? It goes *ch-ch-ch* every time you hit total. It really reminds me of the grocery stores when I was a kid. They used to put your groceries in those thick brown paper bags that you could use for book covers later. 

But, um... yeah, because of all this, I’ve also had to cut back on my custom work. I just keep missing my repair deadlines, and when I sit down for client consultations, I just completely lose track of what we're supposed to be designing. Which is such a shame, because sketching the custom pieces is my favorite part. I use these special graphite pencils I order all the way from Germany for my sketches. My grandfather was actually from Germany. He came over when he was just a little boy and he used to carve these incredible wooden toys by hand. I still have a little wooden horse he made me, sitting right on my nightstand next to my reading lamp. The bulb in that lamp just went out last night, actually, and I was looking all over the house for a replacement, but I think we only have those harsh white LED ones left in the hall closet...
Do you need someone else to manage any of your usual daily responsibilities at home, such as paying bills or taking medications?

Well, no, not really at home. I still manage all of that myself, like the bills and my medications and everything. I keep my pill organizers right by the coffee maker so I don't forget them in the morning. It's one of those fancy espresso machines, actually. My husband got it for me for our anniversary last year because I love making cappuccinos. You have to get the milk froth just right, though, or it's not a real cappuccino. I usually use oat milk because regular dairy has been upsetting my stomach lately. I read this article the other day that said a lot of people develop lactose intolerance when they get older, which makes sense, I guess. My aunt Martha had terrible stomach issues, but she wouldn't stop eating this spicy chili she made. She grew her own jalapeños in the backyard. She had this huge vegetable garden with tomatoes and zucchini and everything. I tried growing tomatoes once, but the squirrels kept eating them right before they got ripe. They are so sneaky, those squirrels... they'd just take one bite out of a tomato and leave the rest sitting there on the vine. It's so frustrating when you put all that work into the soil and the watering... wait, did you ask about my medications? No, I take them on my own.
Have you had formal testing of your memory or thinking abilities since these problems began?

No, I haven't had any kind of formal testing for my memory or anything like that. I mean, nobody's ever suggested it. My regular doctor just checks my blood pressure and listens to my heart, which is fine, I guess. He has this really old stethoscope that looks like it's from the 1950s. I always wonder if those vintage medical instruments are worth anything. You know, people collect all sorts of strange things. We had a guy come into the shop once who collected antique pocket watches, but only the ones made in Switzerland. He had this whole special display case for them at his house, lined with this deep burgundy velvet. Velvet is so hard to keep clean, though. It attracts every single piece of dust and lint in the room. I tried making a velvet dress for my daughter when she was little, for a Christmas pageant, but it was a nightmare to sew. The fabric just keeps slipping under the presser foot of the sewing machine. My sewing machine is actually jammed right now, the bobbin thread keeps bunching up underneath... but anyway, no, no testing.
Have you had to stop doing any routine activities outside of work because of these thinking difficulties?

No, I don't think so. I still do all my usual stuff outside of the shop. Like, I still go to the farmer's market every Sunday morning like I always do. I love getting the fresh flowers there. There's this one vendor who sells the most beautiful orchids, these really delicate white and purple ones. I bought one a few months ago, but orchids are just so incredibly fussy to keep alive, you know? You're only supposed to give them, like, one ice cube of water a week, which just feels completely wrong. My grandmother used to have a whole sunroom full of orchids, but she lived down in Florida where the humidity is just out of control. The air there makes your hair frizz up the second you step outside the airport. I went to visit her once in August years ago, and we went to this little seafood restaurant right on the pier, and the seagulls kept swooping down trying to steal our french fries. They are so bold! One of them actually knocked over my entire glass of iced tea right into my lap. It was a total disaster... but, um, wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, stopping my regular activities. No, no, I haven't had to stop doing anything like that.
Has your husband noticed a clear change in your thinking or communication compared with how you were before these problems began?

Well, yeah, he definitely has. That's actually why I came in to see you. Like, someone will come into the shop and ask me a really simple question, like when their ring repair is going to be ready, and I try to answer them, but then my brain just... goes. I'll start talking about the invoices, and then somehow I'm talking about the potting soil I need for the garden, and then the mortgage papers that we need to sign. And I can just look at their faces and see that I'm completely losing them. It's like they're looking at me like I'm speaking a different language. My husband says it's getting worse. He's been trying to help me with the mortgage papers, actually, because the interest rates are just ridiculous right now. We locked in our rate a few years ago, thank goodness, but our neighbors just tried to refinance and they said it was a nightmare. They have this gorgeous house, though, with a wrap-around porch. I always wanted a porch like that, where you could just sit out in the evenings with a glass of lemonade and watch the fireflies. We used to catch fireflies in jars when I was a kid... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, my husband. Yeah, he's noticed it. He's the one who told me I needed to come talk to somebody about it.
Do you find yourself forgetting recent conversations or events, even when you are trying to remember them?

No, I don't think I'm forgetting things like that. I mean, I remember what people tell me, mostly. Like yesterday, my neighbor told me she's getting a new puppy, a golden retriever. They are just the sweetest dogs, aren't they? We had a golden retriever when I was growing up, named Buster. He used to chew on everything, though—table legs, shoes, even the garden hose once. My dad was so mad about that garden hose. He had to go all the way to the hardware store on a Sunday to get a new one, and the hardware store in our town was owned by this grumpy old man who always smelled like pipe tobacco and peppermint. I actually love the smell of pipe tobacco, it reminds me of autumn. Autumn is my favorite season, with all the leaves changing colors. The drive up to the mountains is just breathtaking around October. We took a trip up there a few years ago and stayed in this little cabin that had a wood-burning stove... um, but no, I don't feel like I'm forgetting recent conversations or anything. My memory seems okay.
Have you noticed difficulty completing familiar tasks that require several steps, such as following a recipe or assembling something, even when you are doing them at home?

No, I haven't really noticed any trouble with that. I can still cook and follow recipes just fine. Actually, I made this incredible beef stew just last night. I used my grandmother's old cast iron Dutch oven. You know, those things weigh an absolute ton, but they cook everything so perfectly. I've had that pot for probably twenty years, and it's seasoned so well now that nothing ever sticks to it. I usually buy my stew meat from the butcher down the street, this guy named Sal. He always saves the best cuts for me. He’s been talking about retiring soon, though, and moving out to Arizona. I can't imagine living in Arizona, it's just so brown and dry all the time. I need to be around trees and green grass, you know? Like the park across from our house. They just planted these beautiful new cherry blossom trees there last spring, and I can't wait to see them bloom again. The pink petals just sort of drift down like snow when the wind blows... but, um, what were you asking about? Oh, right, familiar tasks. No, I haven't had any trouble doing things like cooking or putting things together at home.
Do you lose track of conversations in settings outside of work, such as when speaking with family or friends?

Well, yeah, it happens everywhere, not just at the shop. Like I was saying before, that's the whole reason I'm here. It's just so frustrating. Even with my husband or my sister, they'll ask me something simple, just like the customers asking about their ring repairs, and I try to answer, but my brain just takes off. I'll start talking about the invoices from work, and then suddenly I'm going on about the potting soil I need to pick up for the tomatoes, and then I'm stressing about the mortgage papers. My sister came over for coffee on Sunday, actually. We always have coffee on Sunday mornings, it's a tradition we started after our mom passed away. Mom used to make the best coffee cake, with this thick crumb topping that was mostly butter and brown sugar. I've tried to recreate the recipe, but it never comes out quite right. I think it's because she used this specific brand of flour that you can't even find anymore. It's a shame how many good products just disappear from the shelves these days. You go to the grocery store and everything is different... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, losing track of conversations. Yeah, I can just see it in their eyes, whether it's a customer or my sister. I can see them losing me, like they have no idea how I got from point A to point B. It happens all the time now.
Have you ever completed a structured memory or thinking assessment that showed a measurable decline from your previous level of ability?

No, I haven't ever done anything like that. A structured memory test? No. I mean, the only tests I've really taken since college were the ones for my jeweler's certification. That was years ago, though. I had to identify all these different cuts and clarify grades under a loupe. It's fascinating how a tiny inclusion can completely change the value of a stone. I actually prefer working with sapphires over diamonds, to be honest. The deep blue ones from Ceylon—well, Sri Lanka now—they just have this incredible depth to them. I made a custom pendant with a sapphire last month for a client's anniversary. She wanted it set in rose gold, which is so popular right now. Rose gold is just gold mixed with copper, really. It tarnishes a bit differently than yellow gold, but it has that warm tone. My grandmother had a rose gold locket with a picture of my grandfather in his navy uniform... um, but no, I've never had any kind of memory assessment or anything like that done.
Do you have difficulty planning or organizing tasks that you used to manage easily?

Well, yes, actually. I've had to cut back a lot on the custom work at the shop. I just keep missing the repair deadlines, which is awful because people get so attached to their jewelry. And during client consultations, I just... I lose track of what we're doing. It's embarrassing. I even have to get my husband to double-check all the invoices now, and I used to handle all of that myself without a second thought. He's been really good about it, though. He usually sits at the kitchen table with his reading glasses on—he just got these new bifocals that make his eyes look huge, it's kind of funny. We got them at that optometrist next to the bakery. The bakery that makes those amazing little fruit tarts with the kiwi and the glaze. I haven't had one of those in ages. We should probably go this weekend... but, um, what were we talking about? Oh, organizing tasks. Yeah, I just can't seem to manage the shop stuff the way I used to.
When you work alone on a task, do you also lose focus and jump between activities, or does this mainly happen while you are talking with someone?

Well, it happens when I'm alone, too, but I notice it the most when I'm talking to someone. Like I mentioned before, that's really why I came in to see you. A customer will ask me something so simple, like when their ring repair will be ready, and I try to tell them, but my answer just starts going from the shop invoices to the garden soil I need, and then suddenly I'm talking about the mortgage papers. The mortgage papers are such a headache right now, honestly. The bank keeps sending these letters with all this fine print, and they use that terrible recycled paper that feels like sandpaper. I hate touching it. It reminds me of the sandpaper my dad used to use in his woodshop. He made these beautiful birdhouses, just out of scrap wood he'd find. He painted one bright red to attract cardinals, because cardinals are supposed to be a sign that angels are near. I haven't seen a cardinal in my yard all winter, though. Mostly just those little brown sparrows that eat all the seed out of the feeder before the bigger birds even get a chance... um, but yeah. I can just see it in people's faces when I'm trying to answer them. I can see them losing me because my mind just jumps all over the place.
Has your husband noticed you forgetting recent information or conversations?

No, I don't think so. He hasn't mentioned me forgetting things we just talked about or anything like that. I mean, we always catch up in the evenings while I'm making dinner, and he usually tells me about his day. He works over at the hardware store, mostly in the paint department lately. They have this huge machine that shakes and mixes the custom colors, and it's just so loud. I went in there once to get a specific shade of teal for our guest bathroom, and the smell of the paint base was just awful. We ended up going with wallpaper instead. It has these little silver vines on it that catch the light perfectly in the morning. I had to order it special from a place in New York. New York is so overwhelming, though, all those people and the noise. We went there for our honeymoon, actually, and took one of those carriage rides through Central Park, which was freezing because it was November... um, but no, to answer your question, he hasn't said anything about my memory for recent things. It's really just the focus and getting off track, like I said.
Have you noticed difficulty remembering newly learned information, such as information someone told you earlier that day?

No, I haven't really noticed any problems with remembering things people just told me. It's more just the keeping my train of thought straight. Like, if one of my suppliers calls and tells me they're out of a certain gauge of silver wire, I remember that fine. I'll just write it down on one of those little yellow sticky notes. I have a whole pad of them right next to the phone. They're actually shaped like little daisies, which I thought was so cute when I bought them at that stationary store downtown. The one with the green awning? It's right next to the coffee shop that roasts their own beans. The smell when you walk by is just incredible, especially on a rainy day. I love rainy days, honestly. The sound of the rain on the roof of the shop is so peaceful, it almost makes me forget how behind I am on everything... but, um, no, I don't think I have trouble remembering new things people tell me. Just the focus part.
When you notice your thoughts drifting off topic, are you able to deliberately bring your attention back to the question you were answering?

I try to, but... no, not really. Like I was telling you earlier, that's the whole reason I'm here. Once I start drifting from a simple question about a ring repair over to the shop invoices, and then the garden soil and the mortgage papers... I just can't rein it back in. I just watch myself doing it and I can see the customer completely losing me. It’s like watching a train go off the tracks. I used to take the train to visit my aunt in Chicago when I was little. The seats were covered in this scratchy green velvet, and the conductor had this beautiful shiny pocket watch. I love antique pocket watches. Working with the tiny gears as a jeweler is actually really soothing, though you need such a steady hand and a good magnifying loupe. Mine has a little tiny scratch in the corner of the lens right now, which is so annoying when I'm trying to set a small stone... um, but no, to answer your question, once my thoughts start jumping like that, I can't seem to just stop and deliberately get back to the actual question.
Is your main difficulty organizing and controlling your thoughts and actions, rather than forgetting information?

Yes, exactly. That's exactly it. It's not that I'm forgetting things, it's just... I came in because when people ask me a simple question, like when a ring repair will be ready, my answer starts going from the shop invoices to the garden soil I need to buy, and then to the mortgage papers. I can see them completely losing me. It's so frustrating because I know the answer, I just can't seem to get it out straight. Garden soil is getting so expensive, by the way. I used to buy it in bulk from this nursery out on Route 9, but they closed down last spring. The owner, Mr. Henderson, retired and moved down to Florida. I think he said Sarasota? Or maybe Naples. Naples has those beautiful white sand beaches, though the humidity down there just ruins my hair. I tried using this special anti-frizz serum once, but it just made everything look greasy. Greasy hair is the worst when you're working under those bright jeweler's lamps all day... but yes, it's the organizing my thoughts that's the problem, not my memory.
Do you find it difficult to stop yourself from saying an irrelevant thought once it comes to mind?

Yeah, it's... it's like I have no brakes. Once the thought is there, it just spills out. Like I said before, someone will just ask about a simple ring repair, and before I know it, I'm talking about shop invoices, and then I'm on about the garden soil I need, and then somehow I'm talking about the mortgage papers. And I can just see the look on their face, you know? They're completely lost. It's so embarrassing. Speaking of mortgage papers, the bank sent me this letter last week that was printed on the thickest, most beautiful paper. It had this subtle watermark of an oak tree. I love oak trees. We had this massive one in our front yard when I was growing up, and my dad built a tire swing on the lowest branch. He used this thick, yellow nylon rope that would always leave little splinters in my hands if I gripped it too tight. I had to use tweezers to get them out, the same tweezers I use now for placing tiny diamonds in settings. They're precision-tipped, made in Switzerland... but, um, yeah. I just can't stop the thoughts from coming out once they pop into my head.
Have you experienced any other new neurological symptoms, such as changes in speech, balance, strength, or coordination?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My balance is fine, and my hands are still strong enough to work the metal... well, as strong as they need to be for jewelry, anyway. It's not like I'm a blacksmith. There's this blacksmith down at the historical village who does demonstrations on weekends. He makes these incredible wrought iron hooks and horseshoes, just pounding away at the anvil. The sound it makes is so loud, just this sharp *ping* that echoes across the whole field. They sell kettle corn right next to his stall, and the smell of the sugar melting is just heavenly. I tried making kettle corn at home once, but I burnt the sugar to the bottom of my favorite stainless steel pot. I had to scrub it for an hour with baking soda and vinegar. Vinegar is actually really good for cleaning silver, too, if you mix it with a little salt and wrap it in aluminum foil... but no, physically, I feel completely normal. No changes in my speech or coordination or anything. Just the thoughts getting all tangled up.

doctor.intent: Understand the patient's main reason for seeking care
doctor.question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
target_item.manifestation: I came in because when people ask me a simple question, like when a ring repair will be ready, my answer starts going from invoices to garden soil to the mortgage papers and I can see them losing me.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code (S021).

patient.answer: Hi. Well, I came in because... it's just getting really hard at work. I make and repair jewelry, you know? And lately, when someone asks me a simple question, like, "When will my ring repair be ready?" I try to answer, but my brain just... goes somewhere else. I'll start talking about their invoice, and then somehow I'm talking about the potting soil I bought for my garden, which reminds me of the mortgage papers I need to sign, and...
